acv.quote: It would have been about seventy-five K a year.

data.reason: Diane, the CFO, froze all new vendor projects after a missed Q3. Owen had no payback number of Pikeview's own to show her. Renee calls it timing, but that cost case was never built.

trigger.action: Lead with how long a pricing change takes on homegrown billing.
trigger.why: Owen wanted a rebuild because every price change took a quarter, but nothing set a date.
trigger.quote: every pricing change takes them a quarter

decider.action: Show finance why homegrown billing is urgent, not a nice extra.
decider.why: Diane, the CFO, froze the deal and never met us. She only funds what is on fire.
decider.quote: if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded.

competitor.action: Spell out what keeping homegrown billing costs each year.
competitor.why: Renee says the only rival was doing nothing. Near the end, Owen's questions turned to payback for finance.
competitor.quote: do you have something that shows payback?

message.action: Cut 'grow revenue' from the billing pitch.
message.why: Owen loved the price-change demo but pushed back when Renee talked about growing revenue.
message.quote: we're not trying to grow revenue with billing

proof.action: Add a payback example built on one customer's own billing costs.
proof.why: Renee sent the general ROI deck, but Owen needed a Pikeview number to win over Diane.
proof.quote: I can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours.

words.action: Describe homegrown billing as 'a tax on the roadmap'.
words.why: Owen used this phrase for his problem, and it ties to the demo he liked most.
words.quote: stop it being a tax on the roadmap.
